# Controlling Codex from your phone

Chosen approach: **Tailscale (private network) + Windows OpenSSH + a phone SSH client.**
Codex keeps running on this PC against the local repo; the phone is only a terminal.

Why this one:
- No public port and nothing published: the PC is reachable only from your own Tailscale devices.
- The code and `.env` (API key) stay on this machine. The cloud route (Codex in the ChatGPT app)
  needs the repo pushed to GitHub, and this repo has no remote.
- No custom bridge code (Telegram bot, web shell), so there's nothing new to secure.

## One-time setup on the PC (elevated PowerShell)

```powershell
# 1. Private network
winget install Tailscale.Tailscale
tailscale up            # sign in; note the machine name, e.g. my-pc

# 2. SSH server (Windows optional feature)
Add-WindowsCapability -Online -Name OpenSSH.Server~~~~0.0.1.0
Start-Service sshd
Set-Service sshd -StartupType Automatic

# 3. Codex CLI (skip if `codex --version` already works)
npm install -g @openai/codex
```

Lock SSH down to keys only: put your phone's public key in
`C:\ProgramData\ssh\administrators_authorized_keys` if your account is an admin, otherwise in
`~\.ssh\authorized_keys`. Then set `PasswordAuthentication no` in
`C:\ProgramData\ssh\sshd_config` and run `Restart-Service sshd`.

## On the phone

1. Install Tailscale and sign in with the same account.
2. Install an SSH client (Termius, or Blink on iOS) and generate a key. Its public key goes into the file above.
3. Connect to `Ikran@my-pc` (the Tailscale name), then:

```powershell
cd <path-to-this-repo>
codex
```

## Caveats

- **Session dies when the phone disconnects.** Windows has no tmux. For long tasks, either SSH into
  WSL and run `tmux new -As codex` there (reattach later with the same command), or use
  non-interactive runs: `codex exec "fix the failing test" > codex.log` and check the log afterwards.
- Anyone on your tailnet can reach port 22. Keep the tailnet to your own devices, or add a Tailscale ACL.

I've written a setup guide, but nothing is set up yet. The setup opens remote access to your PC, so I stopped before running any of it.

**Open it:** `start docs\phone-control.md`

1. **The approach:** Tailscale (a private network between your own devices) plus the SSH server built into Windows, and an SSH app on your phone (Termius, or Blink on iOS). You connect from the phone and run `codex` in the repo on your PC. Nothing is reachable from the public internet, and your code and the `.env` API key stay on the PC.
2. **The other option, and why I didn't pick it:** you can run Codex from the ChatGPT phone app, but that runs in OpenAI's cloud against a GitHub repo. This repo has no remote, so it would mean publishing your code. I also skipped a homemade Telegram bot or web shell, because that would be new code that can run commands on your PC.
3. **What I didn't check:** my permission settings blocked the commands that look for Codex, Tailscale and the SSH server, so I couldn't confirm what's installed. I also didn't read `.env`.
4. **What I didn't run:** installing Tailscale, turning on SSH, editing the SSH config and signing in all change your system's security, so they need your OK.
5. **One catch:** Windows has no tmux, a tool that keeps a terminal session alive after you disconnect. If your phone loses connection, Codex stops. The guide covers two workarounds: running it inside WSL with tmux, or running Codex in the background (`codex exec ... > codex.log`) and reading the log later.

Reply "go" and I'll run the PC setup from the guide. You'll still need to sign in to Tailscale and add your phone's SSH key yourself. Or tell me if you'd rather use the cloud route from item 2.
